title: Choose the Clicker Generator's layout
question: The world is settled (Swatch Wall). The roll dealt three ways to organise the tool page; Spec Sheet leads. Lock one, or re-roll.

options.label: Spec Sheet
options.lineage: a printed spec sheet pinned beside the bench
options.thesis: Every parameter is a row on one printed spec sheet; the 3D bench sits beside it and the sheet's black tab exports.
options.viewport: Shell: brand pin top-left, tool title pin beside it, undo/redo pin top-right. Left 58%: the bench, a recessed charcoal build plate holding the live clicker, with a small floating toolbar (Assembled / Exploded / Show switch / Cut open). Right 42%: one PLA-white spec sheet hanging on a peg, sectioned DESIGN (source tabs Text / SVG / Image, the text field), FOOTPRINT (size digits + slider, style, margin), SWITCH & FIT (cutout, pocket, clearance), FINISH (colour chips, keychain). Fixed-digit readouts on every numeric row. Sheet foot: black tab Download 3MF, quiet STL zip link. Warnings appear as a vermilion-free orange slip clipped to the sheet. Signature move: the control panel is literally a printed sheet; sections are ruled, readouts are digit tiles.
options.risk: Dense by design; on phones the sheet stacks under the bench and gets long. Needs disciplined section rhythm or it reads as a form.

options.label: Bottom Drawer
options.lineage: a console: the model fills the screen, controls rise from a drawer
options.thesis: The model is the page; a tabbed drawer rises from the bottom edge with one group of controls at a time.
options.viewport: Shell: a thin top strip (brand pin, tool title, undo/redo, Download 3MF tab at the far right). The bench fills everything below: full-bleed charcoal build plate with the clicker large, floating view toolbar top-centre. From the bottom edge a PLA-white drawer rises ~240 px with tabs Design / Shape / Fit / Finish along its top edge; the active tab shows its controls in one horizontal strip of fields with digit readouts. Collapsing the drawer leaves a tab rail. Same organisation on phones (drawer becomes a sheet). Signature move: the drawer is a swatch card sliding up from the board's bottom edge.
options.risk: One group visible at a time hides relationships (size vs. fit); the horizontal strip gets cramped with 6+ controls.

options.label: Bench & Rail
options.lineage: the classic configurator: a control column beside a bench
options.thesis: A single left column of collapsible groups beside a full-height bench, export floating at the bench's corner.
options.viewport: Shell: left column 360 px as a stack of hanging cards: an orange header card (CLICKER, text field, source tabs) and PLA-white group cards (Footprint, Switch & fit, Finish), one open at a time with a status line in each closed header. Right: the bench full height, charcoal plate, floating view toolbar top-centre, an export dock bottom-right (black Download 3MF tab, STL zip, save/load icons). Undo/redo in the column foot. Phones: bench on top (45vh), column becomes an accordion below. Signature move: each control group is its own swatch on the board.
options.risk: The most familiar configurator shape; distinctiveness rests entirely on the materials and the readouts.

options.label: Acetate Manual
options.lineage: boxed-software reference manual with acetate leaves
options.thesis: Controls on clear leaves hinged over a coloured section board, a stepped tab rail down the edge.
options.viewport: A tab rail of sections; the open section's leaf carries its controls.
options.case: Loses both axes: makers don't identify with 1990s software manuals, and leaves-over-board is a costume for a working screen.
options.kept: One rank of elevation: controls sit on one card above the board, never cards on cards.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Terrain fixed beneath, the course rides above in purple.
options.viewport: A fixed-scale map with a purple course and a ranked legend.
options.case: Loses both axes: no tie to printing; a map metaphor obscures a configurator.
options.kept: The overlay never edits the terrain: the reference switch and cut-open view are preview layers that never change the exported geometry.

options.label: Streaming Wall
options.thesis: Rows of tiles; the focused one grows and tells you what it is.
options.viewport: Horizontal rows of poster tiles on a dark wall.
options.case: Loses both axes: a browsing wall, not a configurator; dark neutral ground contradicts the world.
options.kept: A focused sample tile expands to show its spec before you load it.

options.label: Plate Section
options.lineage: design annual plate section on uncoated stock
options.thesis: Registration furniture around plates on near-white paper.
options.viewport: A near-white sheet with registration marks and a periwinkle stamp.
options.case: Loses both axes: near-white editorial stock replaces the committed board; nothing for the task.
options.kept: Registration marks become real dimension callouts (mm) drawn on the bench.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built cell by cell on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: A visible grid with monumental grid-built letterforms.
options.case: Loses both axes: a type-specimen page, not a tool; grid-built letters would misrepresent the traced relief.
options.kept: The build-plate grid is a real toggleable state, not decoration.

options.label: Split-flap Board
options.thesis: Fixed character cells that flip; every change is a cascade.
options.viewport: A ruled board of flap rows and columns.
options.case: Holds audience interest (makers love split-flaps) but loses product clarity: an instrument's face on a working screen is a costume, and the world already owns fixed-digit readouts.
options.kept: Loading a preset cascades the digit readouts one tile at a time, so a change is a visible event.
